title: Nasdaq, S&P 500 end lower as investors assess Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia
summary: The Nasdaq and S&P 500 indices experienced a drop as Nvidia and other tech shares fell. Investors reacted to potential new tariffs, raising concerns about market stability. Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang was reinstated, which had previously spurred a market rally. In contrast, the Dow Jones Industrial Average saw gains amid varied sector performances. Anticipation for the upcoming Personal Consumption Expenditures report added further uncertainty to investor sentiment.

title: PE/VC investments in India surge to USD 8.7 billion in October, highest monthly level in five years: EY-IVCA report
summary: Private equity and venture capital investments in India surged to USD 8.7 billion in October 2026. This monthly figure is the highest recorded in the past five years, supported by eight large deals totaling USD 7.3 billion. Financial services attracted the majority of investments, amounting to USD 5.9 billion during this period. Despite the increase in investments, exit activity declined, with 21 exits valued at USD 544 million.

title: Nasdaq, S&P 500 end lower as investors assess Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia: US Stock Market Highlights
Shift in pension and insurance money to equities dampens long-term G-sec demand: RBI DG
summary: The demand for long-term government securities has seen a marginal decline recently. Insurance companies and pension funds are increasingly focusing on equities instead of sovereign debt. This change has impacted the stability of the government securities market and highlighted challenges in liquidity distribution. The Reserve Bank of India emphasizes the need for a coordinated approach and broader participation from institutional investors.

title: A 50 bps jumbo rate hike can lead to financial stability concerns, hurt growth: Report
summary: SBI economists have lowered their rate hike expectations for the upcoming RBI policy review. They now anticipate a 0.25 per cent increase rather than the previously expected 0.50 per cent. This adjustment stems from concerns regarding financial stability and potential impacts on economic growth. The RBI's monetary policy committee is scheduled to meet from December 2 to December 4.

title: AI boom looms over Warsh's Fed as inflation worries grow
summary: Chairman Kevin Warsh of the Federal Reserve underscores the transformative impact of artificial intelligence on the economic landscape. While he conveys measured optimism about AI's benefits, he also warns of inflationary risks associated with its advancement. Recent discussions outline the challenges faced by Fed officials in navigating economic fluctuations linked to AI investments.

title: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei sells shares worth USD 280.41 million following IPO
summary: Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic, sold shares worth USD 280.41 million after the company's IPO. He reported holding 202.8 million shares and additional shares through trusts. Anthropic's initial public offering raised USD 81.34 billion and made its Nasdaq debut last week. However, the stock price experienced fluctuations, closing down from its opening price. Despite the decline, shares remained above their initial offering price of USD 83.

title: RBI DG asks primary dealers to bid responsibly in G-Sec underwriting auctions
summary: RBI Deputy Governor Rohit Jain has urged primary dealers to bid responsibly in government securities auctions. Jain noted instances of volatile pricing that misalign with orderly market conditions, impacting government borrowing costs. He highlighted the challenge of liquidity concentration in a few securities and called for improved market-making activities. Jain also pointed out declining demand from institutional investors for long-term sovereign debt amid uncertain interest rates.

title: IIFCL IPO: Govt plans to sell part of its stake, company to issue fresh shares
summary: The government aims to partially divest its shareholding in India Infrastructure Finance Company Ltd through an initial public offering. The IPO is expected to occur by the end of the current fiscal year, according to an official statement. IIFCL will issue fresh shares to raise capital alongside the government stake sale. The proceeds from the stake sale will contribute to the government's disinvestment revenue.

title: Investors mint Rs 34.61 lakh cr in November as markets rally nearly 11%
summary: In a remarkable surge this month, Indian equity markets have observed a substantial upswing, with the BSE Sensex climbing nearly 11 percent. This rally was largely propelled by foreign institutional investors, who contributed record-setting inflows exceeding Rs 1 lakh crore. Motivated by lower crude oil prices and impressive Q2 earnings, investor optimism soared, although a recent profit booking saw a minor dip of nearly 2 percent.

title: HDFC Bank, Reliance Industries among 10 stocks with highest DII holding in Q2. See full list
summary: With the rise in the share of MFs and also an overall net investment of Rs 1.69 lakh crore during the quarter, the share of Domestic Institutional Investors (DIIs) as a whole increased to an all-time high of 19.31% as on September 30, 2026, up from 19.16% as on June 30, 2026. Here are 10 stocks with the highest DII holding in the September quarter.

title: The LTCG debate: Why markets need tax stability and not ad-hoc fixes
summary: Foreign Institutional Investor capital is leaving Indian markets, raising concerns over the unpredictability of tax policies. Investors are urging for the reconsideration of Long-Term Capital Gains tax provisions. Historical changes in LTCG have created volatility that affects long-term investors negatively. A stable tax policy framework is essential to attract and retain investment in the Indian financial market.

title: Bitcoin fails to hold Nvidia bump with crypto headwinds in focus
summary: Bitcoin's recent 1% decline has overshadowed positive developments from Nvidia, leading to a dip in investor confidence. The fallout from the Binance hack and notable ETF outflows has further complicated the situation. With the Federal Reserve's potential rate hikes looming in December, many investors are hesitant, preferring to wait for clearer recovery signals despite attractive buying opportunities at current levels, erasing much of Bitcoin's value since its October 2025 peak.

title: South Korea’s Kospi rockets 8% as AI-linked stocks get breather after Jensen Huang’s return as Nvidia CEO. Worst over?
summary: South Korean shares have bounced back sharply after previously hitting a ten-month low, with the KOSPI index climbing 7.19%. This surge was largely driven by a rebound in technology stocks, particularly following Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's return to leadership. Notable AI companies such as Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix recorded substantial gains, while foreign investments showed a positive trend with net purchases totaling 497.3 billion won.

title: Japanese bond yields fall as lower oil prices ease inflation concerns
summary: Japanese government bond yields declined due to falling oil prices that eased inflation concerns. The 10-year JGB yield reached a two-week low of 2.715%. Meanwhile, Japan's benchmark Nikkei 225 index experienced a brief surge of 5% following Nvidia's leadership announcement. Shorter-dated US Treasury yields increased as market stability was reassured by the news. Additionally, markets anticipate a 25-basis-point Federal Reserve rate hike in December.

title: Dollar climbs as renewed AI euphoria fuels Fed hike bets
summary: The dollar is approaching a 20-month peak, thanks to the reinstatement of Nvidia's CEO, which has instilled confidence in the markets. Meanwhile, the euro and sterling struggle against the strong dollar, with the euro hovering near an 18-month low. The market forecasts a Fed rate hike, adjusting to anticipated shifts in monetary policy.

title: Asian stocks rally as Huang's Nvidia return revives AI trade
summary: Asian shares saw significant gains as Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang made a return that relieved market fears. The MSCI Asia-Pacific index rose by 4.6%, while Japan's Nikkei gained 4.5% after a local holiday. This movement followed a 31.5% surge in Nvidia shares, revealing optimism in the beleaguered AI sector. United States Treasury yields climbed alongside the dollar, signaling increased confidence in Fed tightening measures.

title: India’s rupee has become an accidental carry star
summary: The Reserve Bank of India has made moves that temporarily attract carry traders to the rupee. Recent factors include decreasing oil prices and a shift in foreign investment from artificial intelligence stocks to Indian markets. However, these RBI incentives may not last, leaving uncertainty for traders. India's interest rate advantage has significantly diminished since 2011, raising concerns. Policymakers face challenges in ensuring sustained interest in the rupee amid historical depreciation.

title: Wall Street soars on Huang's return to Nvidia, Treasury yields rise
summary: US stocks rebounded sharply on Monday after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive following pressure from President Donald Trump, reversing part of last week’s tech-led market rout. Nvidia jumped 31%, helping the Nasdaq 100 rise 6.5% and the S&P 500 4.7%, while Treasury yields and the dollar also climbed as investors reassessed both AI-sector sentiment and the Federal Reserve outlook.

title: NSEL releases Rs 1,950 crore in one-time settlement, ends 14-year payment default
summary: The National Spot Exchange Ltd has revealed a substantial settlement payout of Rs 1,950 crore to eligible claimants, marking the end of a lengthy 14-year legal battle stemming from a Rs 5,600 crore payment crisis. This settlement received the green light from the Mumbai bench of the National Company Law Tribunal, buoyed by considerable backing from claimants.

title: Nasdaq surges 6%, Dow soars 1,400 pts as markets rebound on Huang’s return: Stock Market Highlights
Adani Airport raises $300 mn from 360 ONE Asset, taking total equity infusion to $1.35 bn
summary: Adani Airport Holdings Ltd will raise USD 300 million to enhance its presence in India's aviation sector. This investment will contribute to its target of increasing passenger capacity from 96 million to 200 million. The company operates eight airports, handling about 95.3 million passengers in the last fiscal year. The funds will support modernizing existing infrastructure and developing airport cities for commercial activities.

title: Nasdaq futures surge 3% as battered AI stocks gain ground
summary: US stock futures showed a significant rebound on Monday after sharp declines in recent weeks. Investor interest is returning to AI-linked stocks following corrected valuations in the market. Chip stocks led this recovery, with major companies like Nvidia and AMD experiencing notable gains. Analysts remain cautious about confirming a sustainable recovery amid pervasive market concerns.

title: Rupee reversal, debt supply drag India bonds in holiday-shortened week
summary: Indian government bonds fell after the rupee lost its positive momentum against the dollar on Monday. A recent debt sale raised concerns about supply when the Indian states auctioned bonds at higher yields. The rupee also ended down 0.3%, reflecting increased dollar demand from large corporations. Benchmark Brent crude oil prices remained close to $92 a barrel, raising inflation concerns in India.

title: Rupee retreats with stocks as rally takes a breather, positive bias lingers
summary: After a five-day rise, the Indian rupee faced a setback on Monday, driven by heightened dollar demand from major corporations. This shift in momentum was compounded by profit-taking activities. The rupee settled at 92.91 against the dollar, following a peak of 92.44. Additionally, underwhelming local stock performance fueled a bearish outlook for the rupee. Nevertheless, analysts predict a sustained positive sentiment towards stocks and currencies amid ongoing evaluations.

title: German bond yields edge higher as equity rebound eases safe-haven demand
summary: Germany's government bond yields increased marginally on Monday as equity markets began to rebound, leading to diminished interest in safe-haven assets. In the wake of a difficult week for stocks, investors indicated a readiness to engage with riskier assets. The yield on 10-year German bonds rose by 2 basis points, signaling a fall in bond prices.

title: India bonds give up marginal opening gains as profit booking takes over
summary: Indian government bonds fell after initial gains due to profit booking by traders and a sharp rupee decline. The benchmark yield of the 6.94% 2036 bond increased to 7.2185% during trading hours. Last week, the yield had dropped significantly due to lower US Treasury yields and a stronger rupee. Investors now focus on the upcoming Reserve Bank of India's policy decision on December 4.

title: Rupee retreats, Goldman calls it a 'port of stability' in AI storm
summary: The Indian rupee initially rose to a seven-month high before retreating amid corporate dollar buying. It is on track for a monthly gain of over 2%, bolstered by significant foreign investment in Indian equities. Analysts noted that the rupee's early gains pushed it into overbought territory, prompting some selling. Despite recent fluctuations, the rupee has remained stable compared to other major currencies.

The great Indian stock market comeback. Can the rally sustain and what should investors do?
summary: Indian equities staged a sharp 9.7% rally in eight sessions through November 12, reversing months of underperformance. A sell-off in US AI stocks, triggered by Republican losses in the midterm elections and fears of tighter AI regulation, spilled across global technology markets. Earlier, foreign investor outflows, elevated crude prices and rupee weakness had weighed heavily on Dalal Street sentiment.

title: India bonds give up marginal opening gains as profit booking takes over
summary: On Monday, Indian government bonds experienced a decline following an initial gain earlier in the day. Traders engaged in profit booking, particularly after last week's significant trends in the market. The Indian rupee sharply fell towards the 93 per US dollar mark, impacting investor sentiment. Additionally, investors are focusing on the Reserve Bank of India's policy decision scheduled for December 4.

title: Global Markets: 5 key triggers to watch this week
summary: Global markets will track five key triggers this week, from Black Friday spending and ECB leadership changes to Asian inflation data, South Korea’s rate decision and business activity.

title: Why is SanDisk stock falling? 5 factors weighing on shares
summary: SanDisk shares plunged amid a broad semiconductor sell-off, with falling NAND price forecasts, weaker storage orders from Chinese cloud companies and concerns over AI spending weighing on sentiment. The stock has lost more than half its value over 30 trading sessions.
